questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Should be avoided because they will distract you.
Should be avoided since other drivers will see you easily.
Are only recommended in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often. You need to know what is behind you at all times. Make mirror checks part of your regular driving routine.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Does not protect your face as effectively as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, a jacket should be worn:

options.text: Only if the ride will be longer than half an hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter the weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from the sun and helps prevent dehydration.

questions.question: If drinking alcohol, you should:

options.text: Decide if you are still fit to ride based on how you feel after you finish drinking.
Set a limit beforehand so you can still safely ride.
Not be concerned about your riding abilities if you feel fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not ride.
questions.explanation: Do not ride after drinking any alcohol. Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: As you slow or stop, you should:

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears with the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should be done:
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. It only takes a few minutes and helps you avoid problems before you start riding.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn
questions.explanation: When your left arm is extended straight out to the left, it means you plan to turn left or change lanes to the left. Hand signals can be used instead of or along with turn signals.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Move to one side of your lane to allow them to share the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow them to pass.
questions.explanation: Let the tailgater pass you. Change lanes safely to let them go ahead. Do not speed up, as this may cause more danger.

questions.question: Which of the following should you inspect during a pre-ride check?

options.text: The general wear and tread of your tires
The amount of cushion your seat has

questions.correctAnswerText: The general wear and tread of your tires
questions.explanation: Before you ride, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, lights, turn signals, brakes, mirrors, clutch, throttle, and horn.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should your clothing do?

options.text: Be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Not fully cover your arms or legs.
Not include a jacket in warm weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect you if you crash.
questions.explanation: Good clothing protects you in a crash. Wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Your clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but loose enough so you can move freely.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. These signs tell you the rules of the road. You must follow them.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: In a position where the driver can see you.
Always on the far left side of the lane.
Always on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a position where the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car. This position makes you most visible in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Which surface is slippery for motorcycles?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wet pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates on the road are all slippery. Ride carefully on these surfaces.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take, and how often should you do it?

options.text: A few minutes, and only once a month.
A few minutes, and before every ride.
Over an hour, and only a mechanic can do it.
Over an hour, and only when carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes, and before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It only takes a few minutes.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, what should riders do?

options.text: Always stay in the same lane position.
Change positions often to avoid boredom.
Pick the position that gives you the most space around you.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pick the position that gives you the most space around you.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly, so the safest lane position also changes. Choose the position that gives you the most space cushion and helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Stops the wheels from locking up and skidding.
Prevents brakes from working on dry roads.
Warns you when brake pads need replacing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops the wheels from locking up and skidding.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents the wheels from locking up and skidding during emergency braking. When electronic sensors detect a wheel is about to lock, the system releases and re-applies brake pressure. This helps you stop safely.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, what should motorcycle riders watch for?

options.text: Cars pulling away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked cars. Drivers may pull away from the curb or leave their parking spaces without warning.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: You can touch the ground with your feet while sitting.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars are above your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch the ground with your feet while sitting.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you if your feet can touch the ground while you sit on it. You should also be able to easily reach and use the controls.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a motorcycle accident?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a helmet.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the single most important thing you can do to reduce your risk of injury or death in an accident.

questions.question: Alcohol does not need to be digested like most food and drinks. What does this mean?

options.text: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the drinker.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body removes alcohol very quickly once it is in your system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the drinker.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested, so it enters the bloodstream quickly and reaches the brain in minutes. The body removes about one drink per hour.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another vehicle, why should you ride in the left portion of your lane?

options.text: It helps you see ahead better.
It makes it harder to see ahead.
It blocks your view of the vehicle in front.
It lets the other driver speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you see ahead better.
questions.explanation: Riding in the left portion of your lane helps you see ahead better and makes other drivers see you more easily.

questions.question: Which of these will NOT help you avoid serious injury in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Have a windshield.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing reduce injury risk when riding a motorcycle. A windshield is not required for safety protection.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down or stopping, at intersections, when changing lanes, and when turning.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no obvious defects, such as cracks or loose padding.

questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks cool.
questions.explanation: Check that your helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly all around your head, and has no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. Appearance is not important for safety.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Always look ahead and watch for possible dangers.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about hazards because there are very few on the road.
Look ahead but try not to look for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always look ahead and watch for possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Always look far ahead to spot potential hazards. This helps you react to dangers before you reach them.

questions.question: What should you do to control your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Keep the motorcycle straight and level.
Look through the turn to see the best path.
Stop completely before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to see the best path.
questions.explanation: To stay in control while turning, look through the turn by turning your head only. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet does NOT need to have:

options.text: An outer shell that resists impact.
An inner lining that absorbs impact.
Bright colors painted on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on the outside.
questions.explanation: A U.S. DOT-approved helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap retention system. Bright colors are not required.

questions.question: What removes alcohol and its effects from your body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time can lower your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers can help you stay awake, but they cannot lower your blood alcohol level or make you sober.

questions.question: What types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.correctAnswerText: Front and rear brakes
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT protective clothing for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Athletic shoes
questions.explanation: In a crash, a leather jacket, denim pants, and full-fingered gloves protect you. Wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes that support your ankles instead of athletic shoes.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Go faster to get off the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, ease off the throttle and go straight. Slow down gradually. If you must brake, gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Should only be used at night.
Does not help other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Reflective material on your vest or helmet makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it day and night.

questions.question: What is the correct way to pass another vehicle?

options.text: You can exceed the speed limit until you finish passing.
You can pass in a no-passing zone if you started in a passing zone.
You can pass on the shoulder.
You must stay within the speed limit and pass only in legal passing zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stay within the speed limit and pass only in legal passing zones.
questions.explanation: Always pass within posted speed limits. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: With the right hand
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip. You control it with your right hand.

questions.question: If your shoes have laces, what should you do with them?
questions.correctAnswerText: Tuck them in.
questions.explanation: Tuck your laces in securely so they do not catch on the motorcycle while you ride.

questions.question: What can happen in a low-speed crash?

options.text: It happens so often there is no need to worry.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be fatal.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can be fatal.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to speed up.
Only when there is heavy traffic.
Any time you plan to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if no one seems to be around.

questions.question: What is the best way to check tire pressure?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge.
questions.explanation: Always use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. A tire can look fine but still be under-inflated. Looking at the tire is not enough.

questions.question: What should you do with your feet when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Keep them firmly on the footrests.
Keep them away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep them firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Place your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not drag them or point your toes down, as they may catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if needed.

questions.question: In a no passing zone, what can a motorcycle do?

options.text: A motorcycle can still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle can pass if it finishes before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle can pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You also cannot pass by riding off the main road.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It helps protect your whole face.
It works less well than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not replace goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: How can common drugs like cold tablets affect riding?

options.text: They can affect your ability to ride safely.
They usually do not affect your ability to ride safely.
They pose no risk to riding.
They are always safe because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can affect your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Most drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can affect your riding skills. Know the side effects of any drug before you ride.

questions.question: If your motorcycle will take longer than usual to stop, what should you do?

options.text: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Decrease the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when riding on slippery surfaces. Give yourself more space if your motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Distances are easier to judge than during the day.
Using a high beam always makes it hard to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down at night and increase your following distance. Use your high beam when there is no other traffic. Be ready to change your lane position for safety.

questions.question: Which helmet type offers the most protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Full-face
questions.explanation: Approved helmets come in one-half, three-quarter, and full-face styles. A full-face helmet gives the best protection.

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It can greatly reduce head injury severity.
It makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can greatly reduce head injury severity.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet greatly lowers your risk of serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet will not limit your side vision.

questions.question: When approaching a bump or pothole, why should you rise slightly off your seat?

options.text: So you can jump off if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you.
So you can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your joints absorb some of the impact force. This keeps you from being thrown off the motorcycle.

questions.question: Why should inexperienced riders ride near the front of a group?

options.text: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
They will get lost if they lead.
They may slow the group down as leaders.
They will ride too fast in any other position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can easily watch them.

questions.question: What is true about an approved helmet?

options.text: It lets you see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
It does not have a chin strap.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets you see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
questions.explanation: Some people think helmets limit vision, but this is not true. A DOT-approved helmet lets you see as far as needed for safe riding.
